jobs.title: Director and Practice Lead, Data Engineering
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital agency and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture.

With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across: Digital Product Strategy & Innovation, Digital Marketing Services, Web & Mobile App Development, Data & AI, Cloud Engineering, and Enterprise Technology Modernization.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location & Flexibility

Our Director & Practice Lead, Data Engineering
will operate remotely in Canada OR be based out of either our Toronto, ON or Vancouver, BC office locations.

The Opportunity

TELUS Digital's Data, AI & Cloud (DAIC) practice is the multidisciplinary engine behind enterprise AI, blending boutique innovation with the breadth of a global services portfolio to help organizations architect, scale, and secure their transformations. Spanning our full family of specialized capabilities, the DAIC practice delivers end-to-end solutions across AI Advisory, AI Solutions, Data & AI Platforms, and Cloud Transformation.

As a premier Google Cloud partner, our Cloud practice is at the forefront of helping enterprises adopt and scale on Google Cloud infrastructure: delivering complex engineering, deployment, and migration programs for some of the largest organizations in Canada and beyond.

The Director & Practice Lead, Data Engineering
will define and own the Data Engineering Practice along with its market positioning, P&L, talent, and the quality of work we deliver for clients. This role is for someone who has led data and AI practices before, understands how to turn messy enterprise data estates into strategic assets, and earns trust with C-suite executives through genuine expertise. You will shape how we help clients move from data ambition to durable, AI-ready infrastructure.

This Role Will Have Four Core Anchor Responsibilities

Strategy: Set the practice vision and align Data & AI capabilities to where enterprise demand is heading.
P&L: Own revenue targets, margin, and growth while being accountable for the practice's full commercial performance.
Talent & Culture: Build a practice where data-driven thinking, innovation, and engineering rigour are the baseline.
Client Impact: Act as a trusted advisor to enterprise CxOs navigating data strategy, AI adoption, and governance.

Responsibilities

Define the multi-year vision for the Data Engineering Practice, ensuring our technical capabilities are ahead of the curve for enterprise demand for Data & AI transformation.
Own the full P&L, including pipeline, pricing, delivery margin, and revenue growth, while reporting directly to executive leadership with clear commercial accountability.
Build and sustain senior relationships with Google Cloud partner teams and client executives to generate meaningful deal flow and expand strategic accounts.
Lead the practice's position on ethical AI and data democratisation while making principled, evidence-based bets on where advanced analytics and AI are creating real enterprise value.
Drive investment in reusable IP, data accelerators, and delivery assets that improve consistency, reduce time-to-value, and protect margins at scale.
Serve as a strategic advisor to client C-suite executives, helping them define data strategy, navigate AI adoption, and build the organisational capabilities to sustain it.
Set the standard for engineering and analytical excellence across the practice by hiring well, developing talent deliberately, and building teams that clients trust and return to.

Competencies

12+ years in data or AI consulting, including at least 3–5 years in a practice leadership or executive role, not just senior delivery or individual contribution.
Proven P&L ownership: Direct experience managing revenue, margin, and growth targets in a consulting or professional services context.
Data and AI ecosystem depth: Strong command of modern data architecture, AI, and ML trends, cloud-native data platforms, and enterprise data governance.
Executive communication: Able to advise, challenge, and build lasting trust with C-suite stakeholders on complex, ambiguous problems, not just present to them.
Business Development track record: Experience generating pipeline and closing complex, multi-stakeholder engagements, not just managing delivery once work is sold.
Talent leadership: Has hired, grown, and retained senior data engineering and consulting talent in a practice or delivery organisation.

Equal Opportunity Employer

At TELUS Digital, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All aspects of employment, including the decision to hire and promote, are based on applicants’ qualifications, merits, competence and performance without regard to any characteristic related to diversity.

We will only use the information you provide to process your application and to produce tracking statistics. Since we do not request personal data deemed sensitive, we ask you to abstain from sharing that information with us.

For more information on how we use your information, see our Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Hamlet of Gjoa Haven - Director of Finance
jobs.description:
About Hamlet of Gjoa Haven

The Hamlet of Gjoa Haven (Uqsuqtuuq) is a northern municipality located on King William Island in the Kitikmeot Region of Nunavut and is home to approximately 1,349 residents. Renowned for its strong Inuit heritage, deep connection to the land and sea, and rich history, Gjoa Haven holds a unique place in the story of Arctic exploration. It is best known as the site where Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen wintered aboard the Gjoa from 1903 to 1906 while completing the first successful navigation of the Northwest Passage. More recently, the waters surrounding King William Island gained international attention with the discoveries of Sir John Franklin's lost expedition ships, HMS Erebus and HMS Terror, found nearby in 2014 and 2016. Today, Gjoa Haven serves as a gateway to Arctic history, culture, and adventure, offering a rare quality of life defined by vast landscapes, abundant wildlife, and a close-knit community. The Hamlet is committed to strong governance, responsible financial management, and the delivery of essential services that support community well-being, infrastructure, public safety, recreation, and sustainable development. Equally important is the Hamlet's commitment to developing local capacity by training, mentoring, and supporting Inuit employees, creating opportunities for career growth, leadership development, and long-term success within the organization and the community.

Why Gjoa Haven?

This is more than a career move — it's a chance to live and work in one of Canada's most storied Arctic communities. Candidates who join the Hamlet gain:
A true northern experience:
the land and sea, the midnight sun, the aurora, and a slower, community-centred pace of life you won't find anywhere else.
Immersion in Inuit culture and history:
work alongside a community proud of its heritage and its role in Arctic exploration history.
Meaningful impact:
your financial leadership directly shapes the services, infrastructure, and future of a community of just under 1,350 residents — the kind of visible, hands-on impact rarely possible in a larger municipality.
Flexibility to match the north's realities:
the Hamlet is open to discussing a hybrid work arrangement for the right candidate, combining dedicated time on-site in Gjoa Haven with the ability to work remotely for part of the role — offering a balance that supports both community presence and personal flexibility.

About the Role

Reporting to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the Director of Finance plays a critical role in ensuring the Hamlet maintains accurate, transparent, and compliant financial reporting. This position works closely with Mayor and Council, senior management, auditors, and external stakeholders to support decision-making and long-term financial sustainability.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Leadership & Strategy
Oversee all financial operations of the Hamlet, including budgeting, financial reporting, accounts payable/receivable, payroll, and cash management, ensuring compliance with applicable accounting standards and Nunavut municipal regulations.
Develop and monitor annual operating and capital budgets in collaboration with the CAO, Mayor and Council, and department heads.
Provide timely, accurate financial reports and analysis to support Council decision-making and long-term financial sustainability.

Governance & Compliance
Ensure compliance with the Nunavut Hamlets Act, municipal bylaws, and all applicable financial reporting requirements.
Coordinate annual audits and liaise with external auditors, ensuring timely completion and resolution of findings.
Develop, implement, and maintain sound financial policies, procedures, and internal controls.

Stakeholder & Vendor Management
Build and maintain effective working relationships with Mayor and Council, senior management, auditors, government funding partners, and vendors.
Manage vendor and external service provider relationships to ensure value, accountability, and service quality.

Team & Community Leadership
Lead, mentor, and develop finance department staff, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Collaborate cross-departmentally to support infrastructure, public safety, recreation, and sustainable development priorities across the Hamlet.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in accounting or finance.
A CPA designation is considered an asset.
7–10 years of progressive experience in accounting or financial management.
5 years of experience developing and monitoring budgets and preparing financial reports.
Experience implementing and maintaining financial policies, procedures, and internal controls.
Experience managing vendor relationships and external service providers.

This is an existing position with a current vacancy.

To apply for this key role, submit your application to Phelps by clicking: https://phelpsgroup.ca/careers/31518/hamlet-of-gjoa-haven-director-of-finance/apply/

All applications will be reviewed and assessed by experienced Phelps search professionals; we do not use artificial intelligence tools to screen candidates. Only applicants selected for an interview will be contacted.

Qualified candidates may be placed on an eligibility list for consideration for future opportunities.
The Hamlet of Gjoa Haven is committed to fostering a representative and inclusive workforce that reflects the community it serves. Preference may be given to qualified Inuit candidates, particularly beneficiaries enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement, in accordance with the Hamlet's commitment to supporting Inuit employment and participation in the workforce.
To learn more, visit our website at https://phelpsgroup.ca/

This role supports the healthcare brands across the FH Health portfolio (Pollin Fertility, Perennial and Wellness Haus). FH Health was founded by tech entrepreneurs to support Canada’s pandemic response with innovative healthcare solutions. We’ve since evolved into a leading health-tech company that transforms traditional clinic experiences by integrating diagnostics and care through technology. We are proud to support a portfolio of healthcare brands:

Pollin Fertility-A next-generation fertility centre revolutionizing patient experience, safety, and outcomes through advanced technology.
Perennial – Integrated primary and wellness care brought directly to retirement residences, improving seniors' health and quality of life.
Wellness Haus – A physician-led clinic blending evidence-based medicine with cutting-edge wellness care.

Learn more:
www.fhhealth.com
www.pollinfertility.com
www.perennialcare.ca

About the Role

We are seeking a strategic and hands-on Director of Finance to lead and scale our finance function and support the growth and expansion of the business. This role will serve as a key member of the leadership team, partnering closely with the executive team to drive financial performance, support growth initiatives, and shape the company’s long-term strategy. This role will also champion process improvements, automation, and the adoption of modern financial technologies, including AI-driven tools, to transform and elevate the finance function. The successful candidate will bring a forward-thinking, digitally savvy approach to optimizing workflows, enhancing reporting, and enabling smarter, faster decision-making.The ideal candidate is a designated CPA with strong analytical capabilities and a proven track record of building high-performing teams, optimizing financial operations, and enabling data-driven decision-making in a high-growth environment.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Leadership & Strategy
Act as a strategic advisor to the executive team on financial planning, growth, and expansion initiatives
Lead the development of long-term financial strategy aligned with corporate objectives
Translate business strategy into actionable financial plans and performance metrics
Support capital planning, fundraising, and investor relations as needed

Financial Planning & Analysis
Oversee budgeting, forecasting, and financial modeling across all business units
Review financial results and identify key drivers, risks, and opportunities
Develop insights on profitability levers, cost optimization, and revenue growth
Establish KPIs and dashboards to enable real-time, data-driven decision-making
Partner with operations and clinical leaders to align financial and business strategies

Financial Reporting & Controls
Oversee monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting processes
Ensure accuracy and integrity of financial statements in accordance with ASPE
Strengthen internal controls, policies, and financial governance frameworks
Lead audit processes, tax compliance, and coordination with external advisors
Accounting & Finance OperationsProvide oversight of day-to-day accounting operations, including A/R, A/P, payroll, inventory management and treasury
Drive process improvements, automation, and scalability across finance functions by leveraging modern technologies, including AI, to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and insight generation
Ensure compliance with regulatory, tax, and payroll requirements
Oversee financial operations across a multi-entity organizational structure

Team Leadership
Lead, mentor, and develop the finance team, fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement
Build and scale the finance function to support company growth and expansion
Promote cross-functional collaboration across departments
Act as a change agent to reimagine and modernize the finance function from the ground up, delivering strategic insights and building a nimble, high-impact team

Qualifications

CPA designation (required) in good standing
8–12+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including leadership roles
Experience in healthcare, technology, or high-growth environments
Strong background in financial planning & analysis, reporting, and operational finance
Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive strategic initiatives
Experience with ERP systems (preferably Odoo) and financial reporting tools
Deep understanding of ASPE and IFRS standards
Exceptional analytical, communication, and leadership skills
Hands-on, adaptable, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment

Why Join FH Health (Perennial, Pollin and Wellness Haus)?

You’ll be joining a mission-driven, fast-growing organization that’s reimagining healthcare with innovation at its core. This is a unique opportunity to play a leadership role in shaping the financial future of a company making a meaningful impact on patients’ lives.

Apply Now

We look forward to learning more about you. If you're a strategic finance leader passionate about driving growth and innovation in healthcare, we encourage you to apply.

FH Health is an equal opportunity, affirmative action employer. jobs.description:
SETUP
: Mostly remote, only required 1-2 times/month in office. Located in North York, ON

CONTRACT
: 18 months

About the Opportunity

Financial Reporting & Consolidations:
Lead the preparation and review of monthly, quarterly, and annual consolidated financial statements and management reporting.
Oversee the consolidation of multiple legal entities/business units, including intercompany balances, eliminations, foreign currency translation, and consolidation adjustments.
Ensure financial reporting is accurate, complete, appropriately supported, and delivered within established reporting timelines.
Maintain and enhance consolidation processes, reporting packages, and financial controls.
Partner with business units and finance teams to resolve consolidation and reporting issues.

US GAAP & IFRS:
Serve as a key technical accounting resource for matters involving US GAAP and IFRS.
Research and assess complex accounting issues and provide recommendations regarding appropriate accounting treatment.
Monitor new and emerging accounting standards and assess their impact on the organization.
Lead the implementation of new accounting standards and changes to existing reporting requirements.
Prepare and review technical accounting memos, position papers, and supporting documentation.
Support accounting matters involving areas such as revenue recognition, leases, business combinations, foreign currency, impairment, and other complex transactions, as applicable.

Controls, Audit & Compliance:
Maintain a strong financial control environment across the reporting and consolidation processes.
Coordinate with internal and external auditors and support quarterly and annual audit requirements.
Ensure appropriate documentation and supporting schedules are maintained for significant accounting judgments, estimates, and transactions.
Identify reporting and control risks and implement process improvements to strengthen financial governance.
Leadership & Business Partnership:
Lead, coach, and develop a team of 4–5 finance and accounting professionals, establishing clear responsibilities and development priorities.
Provide technical guidance and oversight to the team while promoting accountability and high-quality execution.
Partner closely with FP&A, Corporate Accounting, Tax, Treasury, and other finance functions to ensure consistency and accuracy across financial reporting.
Work with senior leadership to communicate financial reporting matters, accounting implications, and significant issues.
Support acquisitions, integrations, restructuring activities, and other strategic initiatives from an accounting and reporting perspective.

Process Improvement:
Drive improvements to the financial close, consolidation, and reporting processes with a focus on accuracy, efficiency, standardization, and scalability.
Identify opportunities to automate manual reporting and reconciliation activities.
Strengthen reporting processes, systems, and controls as the organization grows and reporting requirements evolve.

About You

CPA designation.
10+ years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, including significant experience in a leadership capacity.
Strong technical knowledge and practical application of US GAAP and/or IFRS.
Significant experience with multi-entity consolidations, including intercompany eliminations and foreign currency considerations.
Experience leading and developing accounting or financial reporting teams.

About the Opportunity

Financial Reporting & Consolidations:
Lead the preparation and review of monthly, quarterly, and annual consolidated financial statements and management reporting.
Oversee the consolidation of multiple legal entities/business units, including intercompany balances, eliminations, foreign currency translation, and consolidation adjustments.
Ensure financial reporting is accurate, complete, appropriately supported, and delivered within established reporting timelines.
Maintain and enhance consolidation processes, reporting packages, and financial controls.
Partner with business units and finance teams to resolve consolidation and reporting issues.

US GAAP & IFRS:
Serve as a key technical accounting resource for matters involving US GAAP and IFRS.
Research and assess complex accounting issues and provide recommendations regarding appropriate accounting treatment.
Monitor new and emerging accounting standards and assess their impact on the organization.
Lead the implementation of new accounting standards and changes to existing reporting requirements.
Prepare and review technical accounting memos, position papers, and supporting documentation.
Support accounting matters involving areas such as revenue recognition, leases, business combinations, foreign currency, impairment, and other complex transactions, as applicable.

Controls, Audit & Compliance:
Maintain a strong financial control environment across the reporting and consolidation processes.
Coordinate with internal and external auditors and support quarterly and annual audit requirements.
Ensure appropriate documentation and supporting schedules are maintained for significant accounting judgments, estimates, and transactions.
Identify reporting and control risks and implement process improvements to strengthen financial governance.
Leadership & Business Partnership:

Process Improvement:

Strengthen reporting processes, systems, and controls as the organization grows and reporting requirements evolve.

CPA designation.
10+ years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, including significant experience in a leadership capacity.
